uplink.description: Example 1: both digital inputs (ch0 closed, ch1 open) + battery (flags=0x0007) -> one channels entry per channel
uplink._note: reference/upstream-examples.json example 1: ch0_input 1 and ch1_input 0, battery 2.809 V — values taken verbatim from that upstream output, now scoped into channels entries labelled channel0/channel1 instead of the retired contactState2 extra. Conversion unchanged: word !== 0 -> "closed", 0 -> "open". Satisfies analog-interface (membership sees through top-level channels entries).

uplink.description: Both inputs with the states swapped (ch0 open, ch1 closed, flags=0x0007) -> no cross-talk between entries
uplink._note: Synthetic Decentlab v2 frame (upstream example 1 with the two input words exchanged), decoded values cross-checked against reference/upstream-codec.js: ch0_input 0, ch1_input 1. The mirror image of the vector above, so the pair pins that each entry reads only its own channel's word.

uplink.description: Channel-1-only frame (flags=0x0006, channel-0 block deselected) -> single entry still labelled channel1
uplink._note: Synthetic Decentlab v2 frame, decoded values cross-checked against reference/upstream-codec.js: the sensor-flags bitmap selects only the channel-1 input block (bit1) and battery (bit2), so upstream emits ch1_input 1 and no ch0_input. Pins the presence policy: the absent channel gets no entry and the surviving entry keeps its wire index — it is NOT renumbered to channel0.

uplink.description: Example 2: battery-only frame (flags=0x0004) carries no digital-input block -> error
uplink._note: reference/upstream-examples.json example 2: the sensor-flags bitmap selects only the 1-word battery block, so neither input channel is present. Pins the header's policy — the `channels` key is omitted and the frame is rejected rather than emitting an empty channels array.
Decentlab v2 framing rejects a non-v2 version byte.
